_comment: Gates the MATLAB driver CANNOT measure, and therefore does not silently
omit: they run in another language binding, under another compiler, in
another repo, or against a historical pre-fix engine binary that no
longer exists in the tree.  Each entry records the command that produces
it and the date it was captured; the report labels every one of them as
externally sourced, with that date, so a reader can tell at a glance
which numbers `make polval-regen` refreshed and which it did not.
Update protocol: re-run the command, paste the result here, bump
'captured'.  Do NOT copy any of these into the report prose -- the prose

X_KORGER.text: J. Korger, T. Kolb, P. Banzer, A. Aiello, C. Wittmann, C. Marquardt and G. Leuchs, "The polarization properties of a tilted polarizer," Opt. Express 21(22), 27032-27042 (2013)
X_KORGER.gate: EXTERNAL ANCHOR for the off-normal axis convention -- the published experiment that decides between the two candidate constructions
X_KORGER.note: Mueller matrices of a commercial nano-particle polarizer tilted about an in-plane axis, phi = 94.5 deg, theta swept to near grazing. Their Eq. (5)-(6) is the ABSORBING (material-axis) model: ahat = unit(P_A - (P_A.zhat)zhat), E_out = E_in - (E_in.ahat)ahat, i.e. T_A = 1 - ahat ahat^T = that that^T with that = zhat x ahat -- algebraically the rule PolElt now implements. The rejected alternative is Fainman and Shamir's transmitting-axis projection (Appl. Opt. 23, 3188 (1984)), which is what PolElt did before. The two 'coincide only for normal incidence'; the measurement (their Fig. 2c) is that 'only the absorbing model explains the drastic change of the transmitted state of polarization observed when the polarizer is tilted'.

X_VANHARTEN.text: G. van Harten, F. Snik and C. U. Keller, "Polarization properties of real aluminum mirrors I. Influence of the aluminum oxide layer," PASP 121(878), 377-383 (2009)
X_VANHARTEN.gate: EXTERNAL ANCHOR for the thin-film polarization machinery on a DIELECTRIC-ON-METAL stack -- the configuration class a protected mirror belongs to, and the one no previous gate covered
X_VANHARTEN.command: doi:10.1086/599043 (arXiv:0903.2740v1); Table 2 for the indices, Secs. 2-4 for the film thickness, measurement range and accuracy
X_VANHARTEN.note: Chosen because it states BOTH halves: a full Mueller matrix measured by ellipsometry at 14 incidence angles over 6-70 deg and lambda = 500/550/600/650 nm, AND every model input numerically. Their inputs: Al2O3 n_f = 1.61/1.61/1.60/1.60 (+-0.01, Eriksson et al. 1981); Al real index 0.769/0.958/1.200/1.470 (+-0.01, Lide 2008, interpolated); Al imaginary index 5.88/6.30/6.85/7.33 (their Fit 1, fitted WITH the oxide in the model); oxide 4.12 +- 0.08 nm; 220 +- 10 nm Al evaporated on glass. Their model (Eqs 1-6) is the Macleod/Born-and-Wolf characteristic-matrix form. Their index convention is N = n - ik with k >= 0, IDENTICAL to the MACOS convention, so no translation enters -- and it is load-bearing, since the paper reports that the opposite sign made their fitted oxide come out ~50 nm instead of ~4 nm. Driving the engine with THEIR indices is the point: aluminum index tables genuinely disagree (the paper says so and FITS k rather than adopting a table), and a disagreement traceable to index tables is not a machinery error.

X_VH_DEV_D.gate: (a) MACHINERY -- worst engine-vs-publication deviation in the [1,2] normalized Mueller element (diattenuation), over their 4 wavelengths x 6 incidence angles inside their measured range
X_VH_DEV_D.note: model 128, Bench fold rig per angle, the publication's own stack (4.12 nm Al2O3 / 220 nm Al). Compared per RAY at each ray's own incidence cosine, so no single-AOI approximation enters.

X_VH_DEV_RET.gate: (a) MACHINERY -- worst engine-vs-publication retardance deviation, expressed in the SAME normalized Mueller units (the lower 2x2 block carries 2 sqrt(Rp Rs)/(Rp+Rs) times cos/sin of the retardance)

X_VH_ACC.gate: the publication's OWN stated absolute accuracy, per normalized Mueller matrix element (their Sec. 2: "an absolute accuracy of ~1% of element [1,1]") -- the bar the gate tolerance is stated against

X_VH_HEADROOM.gate: how far inside the publication's measurement bar the engine sits (X_VH_ACC / max(X_VH_DEV_D, X_VH_DEV_RET))
X_VH_HEADROOM.note: Both sides implement the same thin-film theory, so agreement is expected at round-off; the publication's error bar is the reference for what the comparison would have had to beat to be meaningful, not the achieved figure.

X_VH_NOOXIDE.gate: NON-VACUITY -- the engine WITH the 4.12 nm oxide, compared against an analytic WITHOUT it, disagrees by more than the publication's own accuracy
X_VH_NOOXIDE.note: This independently reproduces the publication's central claim -- that a ~4 nm oxide must be modelled to describe the mirror's polarization properties. If the anchor could not separate a bare mirror from an oxidized one it would be measuring nothing.

X_VH_50NM.gate: NON-VACUITY -- 4.12 nm vs the historical 50 nm oxide (which the paper attributes to a sign error on the imaginary index) is separable at their accuracy

X_VH_CAPTURED.gate: capture date of the external anchor above

X_2C_FIXTURE_LAMBDA.gate: FINDING -- the wavelength Rx_Cass_FarField actually runs at, against which the Phase-2c coating constants are labelled "Al at 632.8 nm" and the MgF2 thickness "~quarter wave at 632.8 nm"

X_2C_QW_FRAC.gate: FINDING -- the 110 nm MgF2 film expressed in quarter-waves AT THE FIXTURE'S OWN WAVELENGTH (a quarter wave at 1 um in MgF2 is 181.2 nm)
X_2C_QW_FRAC.note: At 632.8 nm the same film is 0.960 quarter-waves, which is what the 2c constants' comments describe.

X_2C_POWER_1000.gate: FINDING -- cross-pol power ratio (MgF2/Al over bare Al) from the INDEPENDENT analytic at the fixture's actual 1 um, near-normal incidence (the ratio is flat over the whole plausible range -- see X_2C_RATIO_FLATNESS)
X_2C_POWER_1000.command: MACOS_resources/mmacos/tools/pol_external_anchor/ -- vh_thinfilm at lambda = 1 um, d_MgF2 = 110 nm
X_2C_POWER_1000.note: To be compared with 6.4225 predicted from the engine's own Jones pupil and 5.4238 measured by macos.pol_contrast_floor: the 2c number is arithmetically CORRECT for the film as configured.

X_2C_POWER_633.gate: FINDING -- the SAME 110 nm film at 632.8 nm (0.96 quarter-waves) instead REDUCES cross-polarized power to 0.18x of bare aluminium
X_2C_POWER_633.command: MACOS_resources/mmacos/tools/pol_external_anchor/ -- vh_thinfilm at lambda = 632.8 nm, d_MgF2 = 110 nm

X_2C_POWER_TRUEQW.gate: FINDING -- a TRUE quarter-wave MgF2 overcoat (181.2 nm at 1 um) SUPPRESSES cross-polarized power to 0.0157x of bare aluminium, i.e. it buys ~1.8 decades rather than costing one
X_2C_POWER_TRUEQW.note: Identical at 632.8 nm and 1 um, as a quarter-wave condition should be. This is the number that reverses the sign of the 2c design-rules sentence.

X_2C_PRED_JONES.gate: FINDING -- cross-pol power ratio predicted from the ENGINE'S OWN Jones pupil on Rx_Cass_FarField via eps_tot = (A-B)/(A+B), A = prod(r_s), B = prod(r_p)
X_2C_PRED_JONES.note: model 256. Agrees with the independent analytic's 6.35 and with pol_contrast_floor's measured 5.4238 (the residual is dark-zone annulus weighting versus a pupil mean), which is what establishes that the 2c pipeline is self-consistent and the issue is the CONFIGURATION's description.

X_2C_MEAS_FLOOR.gate: FINDING -- the same ratio as macos.pol_contrast_floor actually reports (151.3112 / 27.8977)

X_2C_RATIO_FLATNESS.gate: FINDING -- the MgF2/bare-Al cross-power ratio from the independent analytic across the whole plausible near-normal incidence range (1.3 - 5.1 deg), showing the conclusion does not depend on pinning an exact AOI
X_2C_RATIO_FLATNESS.command: MACOS_resources/mmacos/tools/pol_external_anchor/ -- vh_thinfilm at lambda = 1 um, d_MgF2 = 110 nm, swept in AOI
X_2C_RATIO_FLATNESS.note: A per-element AOI was NOT measured: ray_field's .nx/.ny/.nz is the element AXIS normal broadcast to the grid (not the local surface normal on a curved mirror), and the successive-element deviation route returns exactly 90 deg, so neither is usable through this binding. The flatness above is why nothing in the finding depends on it. See vh_cass_probe.m section 1.
